description: TAURARO is a multidisciplinary Nigerian innovation team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are developing ASTRA, an intelligent astronaut health monitoring system combining AI, health assessment, health intelligence and emergency support for space missions. We welcome passionate individuals in software engineering, AI/ML, healthcare, biomedical science, data analysis, research and design who want to build meaningful solutions for humanity's future.
summary:
ORION-MED is an offline-first autonomous astronaut health monitoring and clinical decision support system developed by Team Tauraro for long-duration deep-space missions. Because communication delays with Earth (up to 14–20+ minutes one-way) prevent real-time flight surgeon intervention during medical emergencies, crews need onboard tools to assess health risks independently.

Built with pure HTML5, CSS3, and modular Vanilla JavaScript, ORION-MED runs 100% locally with zero cloud dependency. Crew members log point-of-care vitals—blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose (mg/dL), body temperature (°C), daily sleep, mood, and radiation exposure (mSv)—or import NASA OSDR/LSDA CSV and JSON datasets. A deterministic rule engine grounded in NASA Human Research Program (HRP) Spaceflight Standard Measures and NASA-STD-3001 evaluates single and compound risks, provides plain-language 5-step clinical guidance for non-specialist crew, tracks 7-Sol physiological drift, gamifies daily countermeasures, and generates asynchronous SBAR reports for delayed Earth transmission.
details:
Overview & How It Works

ORION-MED is a zero-latency, offline-first clinical telemetry dashboard designed for astronauts operating beyond Low Earth Orbit—including Deep-Space Transit (0g), Orbital Space Stations (LEO), Lunar Surface Rovers (0.16g), and Mars Habitats (Partial-g).

1. Multi-Modal Health Data Collection & NASA Dataset Ingestion:

Astronauts can manually log point-of-care self-assessments—Blood Pressure (mmHg), Heart Rate (bpm), Blood Glucose (mg/dL), Body Temperature (°C), Daily Sleep (hrs), Mood/Focus (1–10), and Solar Particle Event (SPE) Radiation Dose (mSv)—or import external .CSV and .JSON telemetry records directly from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) and Life Sciences Data Archive (LSDA).

2. Deterministic Rule-Based Clinical Decision Engine (rules-engine.js):

Because deep-space missions face severe Earth communication latency and signal blackouts, cloud-based AI cannot be relied upon for urgent triage. ORION-MED uses a deterministic, zero-hallucination JavaScript rule engine calibrated to NASA HRP Spaceflight Standard Measures and NASA-STD-3001 radiation limits (50 mSv caution and 250 mSv acute SPE storm-shelter thresholds). Beyond single-metric alerts, the engine detects multi-variable compound risks—such as sleep debt + low blood glucose + elevated heart rate—to predict acute fatigue or syncope hours before a clinical emergency occurs.

3. Visual Triage, Longitudinal Drift & Environment Adaptation:

Each vital sign is displayed on a color-coded status card (Nominal, Caution, Critical) alongside its NASA reference range and plotted across a dynamic 7-Sol Longitudinal Drift chart. Switching mission environments automatically updates active spaceflight hazards (Space Radiation, Isolation & Confinement, Distance from Earth, Altered Gravity, and Hostile Closed Environments), cabin baseline conditions, and Earth communication latency.

4. Plain-Language Guidance for Non-Physician Crew & Gamified Adherence:

Recognizing that not every astronaut is a medical doctor, clicking any biomarker opens a plain-language clinical guide answering NASA's five core questions: (1) How to measure in space, (2) Why the exam is needed, (3) Spaceflight hazard link, (4) Escalation thresholds, and (5) Immediate preventive/corrective actions. Proactive check-in prompts, a Crew Readiness Score (0–100%), protocol streaks, and a localStorage-persisted countermeasure checklist encourage daily preventive compliance.

5. Asynchronous SBAR Flight Surgeon Uplink:

When abnormal patterns are detected, ORION-MED generates a standardized Situation, Background, Assessment, and Recommendation (SBAR) medical packet ready for compressed transmission during Earth communication windows.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

- Frontend & Architecture: Semantic HTML5, Modern CSS3 (dark aerospace glassmorphism HUD), and modular Vanilla JavaScript (index.html, style.css, nasa-datasets.js, rules-engine.js, app.js).

- Offline Storage: Browser localStorage for persistent longitudinal logs, streaks, and checklists without external servers.

- Development Tools: VS Code, Git/GitHub, and local Python HTTP server for testing.

Super Intelligence (SI) Transparency Disclosure

Super Intelligence (SI) coding and ideation assistants (Google Gemini and Antigravity) were utilized by Team Tauraro to accelerate UI prototyping, modular JavaScript structuring, and presentation copy drafting. All clinical rules, NASA-STD-3001 threshold mappings, architectural decisions, and final code verification were reviewed and assembled by Team Tauraro without modifying or generating any NASA logos or official insignia.
